question: In which case did the court rule that Parliament CANNOT amend the basic structure of the Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kesavananda Bharti Case**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Kesavananda Bharti case is one of the most significant cases in Indian constitutional history.
 
• In this case, the Supreme Court of India propounded the Basic Structure Doctrine.
 
• The judgement held that while Parliament has wide powers, it cannot amend the basic structure of the Constitution.
 
• The case was decided in 1973 by a 13-judge bench of the Supreme Court.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Balbir Mehta Case**

 
 
• This case is primarily known for its recommendations on Panchayati Raj institutions.
 
• It played a significant role in the development of local self-government in India.
 
 
 
• **Ashok Mehta Case**
 
 
• The Ashok Mehta Committee was set up in 1977 to suggest measures to strengthen Panchayati Raj institutions.
 
• It recommended the constitution of a two-tier Panchayati Raj system.
 
 
 
• **Golaknath Case**
 
 
• The Golaknath case was decided in 1967.
 
• The Supreme Court ruled that Parliament could not curtail any of the Fundamental Rights in the Constitution.
 
• This decision was later overturned by the Kesavananda Bharti case.
